sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: MID/UPPER LEVEL FLOW PATTERN IS EXPECTED TO UNDERGO A CHANGE TODAY AS SWLY WINDS OVER THE CENTRAL STATES TRANSITION TO MORE WSWLY FLOW FROM THE FOUR CORNERS TO GREAT LAKES/OH VALLEY. THIS CHANGE WILL OCCUR AS A MORE PRONOUNCED SHORT WAVE TROUGH MOVES ENEWD FROM THE CENTRAL ROCKIES TO THE MID MO VALLEY BY AFTERNOON AND THEN INTO THE GREAT LAKES REGION TONIGHT. DESPITE WEAK HEIGHT FALLS EXPECTED ACROSS THE SRN PLAINS TO MID MS VALLEY...SEVERAL MID LEVEL IMPULSES WILL TRACK INTO THE MID MS VALLEY TODAY AND ALSO INTO THE SRN PLAINS AIDING TSTM DEVELOPMENT. IN THE LOW LEVELS...AT 12Z...A SURFACE FRONT IS EXPECTED TO EXTEND SSWWD FROM THE WRN GREAT LAKES REGION THROUGH NRN MO TO WRN OK AND THE SRN TX PANHANDLE. THIS BOUNDARY SHOULD MOVE SLOWLY ESEWD TOWARD THE MID MS VALLEY...AND THROUGH THE SRN PLAINS...WITH THE FRONT EXTENDING FROM WRN IL...CENTRAL MO...ERN/SRN OK TO WEST CENTRAL TX BY 28/00Z. GREATER EWD MOVEMENT OF THIS BOUNDARY IS EXPECTED ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES. A SURFACE WAVE ATTENDANT TO CENTRAL ROCKIES TROUGH IS EXPECTED TO TRACK NEWD ALONG THE SURFACE FRONT FROM SRN KS... REACHING NERN MO BY 28/00Z. MODELS SUGGEST CURRENT ONGOING CLUSTERS OF TSTMS/CONVECTIVE COMPLEX OVER OK/KS

sections.title: SRN PLAINS TO LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: ALTHOUGH STRONGER SWLY LLJ IS EXPECTED TO TRANSLATE NEWD ACROSS THE MID MS VALLEY TODAY...30-40 KT SSWLY WINDS SHOULD BE MAINTAINED FROM ERN TX/LOWER MS VALLEY INTO THE OZARKS IN RESPONSE TO APPROACH OF A SHORT WAVE TROUGH FROM NRN MEXICO. THIS LOW LEVEL FLOW WILL MAINTAIN RICH MOISTURE INTO THE WARM SECTOR ACROSS OK/TX WHERE SURFACE DEWPOINTS ARE ALREADY IN THE 60S...WHILE SIMILAR VALUES SPREAD NWD THROUGH THE LOWER MS VALLEY TODAY. STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES EXTENDING FROM TX/OK AT 12Z TODAY WILL SPREAD ENEWD INTO THE LOWER MS VALLEY/OZARKS REGION AIDING IN DESTABILIZATION AS SURFACE HEATING SHOULD OCCUR IN THE WAKE OF THE EARLY MORNING CONVECTION LOCATED TO THE NE OF THIS AREA. GIVEN TIMING OF NRN MEXICO SHORT WAVE TROUGH INTO CENTRAL TX TOWARD 12Z TODAY...MODELS SUGGEST NEW TSTM DEVELOPMENT MAY FORM DURING THE 12-15Z TIME FRAME FROM CENTRAL TX INTO SRN AND POSSIBLY CENTRAL OK. THIS SCENARIO APPEARS POSSIBLE GIVEN THE EXPECTED PRESENCE OF WEAK SURFACE BASED INHIBITION AT 12Z TODAY SUPPORTING SURFACE BASED DEVELOPMENT SOON AFTER THE ONSET OF DIABATIC HEATING AND FORCING FOR ASCENT WITH TROUGH SPREAD ACROSS THE SRN PLAINS. 50 KT SWLY MID LEVEL JET TRANSLATING FROM CENTRAL TX TO E

sections.title: LOWER MO/MID MS VALLEYS TO SRN GREAT LAKES
sections.text: A NARROW CORRIDOR OF SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN THE LOWER-MID 60S ARE EXPECTED TO RETURN NWD ALONG AND AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT THROUGH THE MID MS VALLEY WITH LOWER 60S DEWPOINTS REACHING THE SRN GREAT LAKES. EXTENSIVE CLOUDINESS EXPECTED ACROSS MUCH OF THIS REGION TODAY WILL LIMIT SURFACE HEATING. THIS SHOULD TEND TO LIMIT DESTABILIZATION WITH MLCAPE RANGING FROM 500-1000 J/KG. DESPITE THE MORE MARGINAL INSTABILITY...ESPECIALLY WITH NERN EXTENT...STRONG KINEMATICS ACCOMPANYING EJECTING LEAD SHORT WAVE TROUGH ARE EXPECTED TO PROMOTE ORGANIZED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS ALONG THE COLD FRONT AND ANY OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES LEFT OVER FROM ONGOING MORNING STORMS ACROSS MO TO ERN IA/WRN IL. GIVEN STRENGTH OF SWLY LLJ /40-50 KT/...LOW LEVEL SHEAR /SFC-1 KM SRH 100-200 M2/S2/ WILL SUPPORT ISOLATED TORNADOES IN ADDITION TO A THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL.

sections.title: TX/OK PANHANDLES REGION
sections.text: AN INCREASING SLY LLJ ACROSS W TX MONDAY NIGHT IS EXPECTED TO RESULT IN A STRONG WAA REGIME ALONG AND N OF THE COLD FRONT WHICH SHOULD EXTEND INTO WEST CENTRAL TX BY THIS EVENING. ELEVATED MUCAPE OF AT LEAST 1000 J/KG AND EFFECTIVE SHEAR OF 30-40 KT SUGGESTS HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH STORMS THAT FORM ACROSS THIS AREA BETWEEN 06-12Z. ..PETERS/GARNER.. 04/27/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: POSITIVE TILT RCKYS/NRN PLNS TROUGH WILL SHEAR ENE...IN PIECEMEAL FASHION...INTO THE UPR MS VLY/UPR GRT LKS THIS PERIOD AS UPR RIDGE HOLDS FIRM ALONG THE MID/S ATLANTIC CST. ELSEWHERE...SATELLITE LOOPS SUGGEST THAT A SEPARATE SHORTWAVE IMPULSE NOW APPROACHING THE TX BIG BEND WILL CONTINUE ENE INTO THE LWR MS VLY AS A NEW UPR LOW EVOLVES OVER THE PACIFIC NW. AT LWR LVLS...COLD FRONT TRAILING SW FROM UPR MI SFC LOW SHOULD MOVE STEADILY E/SE ACROSS THE GRT LKS /MID MS VLY...WHILE SWRN PART MOVES SWD INTO WRN/CNTRL TX.

sections.title: SRN/ERN TX TO ARKLATEX TODAY
sections.text: OVERNIGHT ELEVATED CONVECTION OVER THE TX HILL COUNTRY HAS EVOLVED INTO A LOOSELY-ORGANIZED MCS OVER CNTRL TX THIS MORNING. SRN/ERN PORTIONS OF THE SYSTEM EXPECTED TO FORWARD-PROPAGATE E OR ENE INTO 30-40 KT...VERY MOIST LOW LVL SLY FLOW CONTINUING ACROSS SRN AND ERN TX. ALTHOUGH DEEP WIND FIELD WILL WEAKEN OVER THE REGION THROUGH THE DAY AS MAJOR PART OF CNTRL RCKYS TROUGH LIFTS NE INTO KS/NEB... ASCENT PROVIDED BY BIG BEND UPR IMPULSE AND DAYTIME HEATING SHOULD FOSTER VIGOROUS STORM DEVELOPMENT. PREDOMINANT CONVECTIVE MODE SHOULD BE BROKEN LINE SEGMENTS. EMBEDDED LEWPS/SUSTAINED STORMS COULD YIELD DMGG WINDS...HAIL...AND POSSIBLY A COUPLE SHORT-LIVED TORNADOES THROUGH EARLY TONIGHT.

sections.title: COLD FRONT FROM LWR MI SW TO NW TX
sections.text: OVERNIGHT MCS IN TX...AND LEFTOVER STORMS ERN KS/MO...HAVE DISRUPTED CONVERGENCE INTO COLD FRONT TRAILING SW FROM UPR MI SFC LOW. CLOUDS ASSOCIATED WITH BOTH AREAS OF CONVECTION WILL LIMIT PRE-FRONTAL SFC HEATING FOR AT LEAST SOME TIME TODAY. THUS...WHILE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM INVOF FRONT IN RESPONSE TO SFC HEATING LATER TODAY... ACTIVITY LIKELY WILL NOT FORM A CONTINUOUS BAND FROM MI TO TX. IN NW TX...A WINDOW OF OPPORTUNITY MAY EVOLVE LATE THIS AFTN THROUGH EARLY EVE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SMALL CLUSTER OF INTENSE STORMS WITH LARGE HAIL AS SFC HEATING IN WAKE OF CNTRL TX MCS DESTABILIZES MODERATELY SHEARED REGION IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF FRONT/E OF REMNANT DRY LINE. THIS ACTIVITY MAY BUILD/MOVE S ALONG THE DRY LINE INTO THE LOW ROLLING PLNS BEFORE DIMINISHING AFTER SUNSET. DEEP SHEAR WILL INCREASE WITH NWD EXTENT ALONG THE COLD FRONT FROM ERN OK/AR NEWD INTO MI...WHILE INSTABILITY CORRESPONDINGLY DECREASES. A SUFFICIENT COMBINATION OF SHEAR/SFC-BASED INSTABILITY SHOULD EXIST ALONG THE BOUNDARY AND/OR ALONG PREFRONTAL OUTFLOW TO SUPPORT BANDS/SMALL CLUSTERS OF SUSTAINED STORMS/POSSIBLE SUPERCELLS FROM THE ERN HALF OF OK NEWD INTO MO/NRN AR. BACK/VEER PATTERN IN WIND PROFILES A

sections.title: SW TX PANHANDLE/W CNTRL TX/NE NM LATE IN PERIOD
sections.text: SLY LLJ SHOULD STRENGTHEN OVER W TX LATE TONIGHT/EARLY TUE ATOP SHALLOW POST-FRONTAL COOL DOME AS A SRN STREAM IMPULSE NOW OFF THE CA CST APPROACHES REGION. GIVEN RICH MOISTURE NOW PRESENT AHEAD OF FRONT...COMBINATION OF INCREASING WAA...ELEVATED MOISTURE INFLUX /MUCAPE TO 1000 J PER KG/...AND 30-40 KT CLOUD LAYER SHEAR MAY SUPPORT A THREAT FOR HAIL AFTER 06Z. ..CORFIDI/SMITH.. 04/27/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: PRONOUNCED S/WV TROUGH ENTERING CENTRAL PLAINS ATTM EXPECTED TO STEADILY WEAKEN AS IT MOVES NEWD ACROSS UPPER MS VALLEY TONIGHT GIVEN THE DEEPENING OF THE MAIN LONG WAVE TROUGH WRN U.S. COLD FRONT FROM SURFACE LOW LS EXTENDS SWWD THRU NRN MO INTO CENTRAL OK AND THEN SERN NM. A LARGE OVERNIGHT MCS OVER TX HAS CONSIDERABLY DISRUPTED THE LARGER SCALE SYNOPTIC FLOW AND REQUIRES SOME ADJUSTMENTS IN THE OUTLOOK FOR SEVERE STORMS TODAY.

sections.title: LOWER MS VALLEY INTO TX
sections.text: THE SEVERE THREAT ASSOCIATED WITH TX MCS CURRENTLY IS DIMINISHING AS IT ENCOUNTERS A WEAKENING SHEAR ENVIRONMENT AND SURFACE OUTFLOW IS OUTRUNNING THE CONVECTION. WITH HEIGHTS GRADUALLY RISING ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT AND DISRUPTION OF BOUNDARY LAYER IN THE WAKE OF THE MCS...THERE IS SOME UNCERTAINTY AS TO DEGREE OF A RENEWED SEVERE THREAT THIS AFTERNOON. MODEL SOLUTIONS SUPPORT THUNDERSTORMS REDEVELOPING ALONG/AHEAD OF COLD FRONT ERN OK INTO AR THIS AFTERNOON WHERE THERE REMAINS A MOIST AND POTENTIALLY MDTLY UNSTABLE AIRMASS. THEREFORE THE EMPHASIS ON THIS OUTLOOK IS FOR A HIGHER POTENTIAL FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AREA WITH PRIMARY THREAT OF LARGE HAIL. SUFFICIENT DEEP LAYER SHEAR EXISTS FOR ROTATING STORMS WHICH WOULD INCREASE RISK OF ISOLATED TORNADOES AND DAMAGING WINDS. FURTHER SW ACROSS TX THE OUTFLOW FROM CURRENT MCS WILL BE A FOCUS FOR RENEWED STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS DEVELOPING BY MAX HEATING THIS AFTERNOON. SEVERE RISK SHOULD BE MORE ISOLATED GIVEN THE OVERALL WEAKER SHEAR ENVIRONMENT.

sections.title: COLD FRONT FROM LWR MI SW TO LWR MO VALLEY
sections.text: OVERNIGHT MCS IN TX...AND LEFTOVER STORMS ERN KS/MO...HAVE DISRUPTED CONVERGENCE INTO COLD FRONT TRAILING SW FROM LS SFC LOW. CLOUDS ASSOCIATED WITH BOTH AREAS OF CONVECTION WILL LIMIT PRE-FRONTAL SFC HEATING FOR AT LEAST SOME TIME TODAY. THUS...WHILE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM INVOF FRONT IN RESPONSE TO SFC HEATING LATER TODAY... ACTIVITY LIKELY WILL NOT FORM A CONTINUOUS BAND. DEEP SHEAR WILL INCREASE WITH NWD EXTENT ALONG THE COLD FRONT FROM ERN OK/AR NEWD INTO MI...WHILE INSTABILITY CORRESPONDINGLY DECREASES. A SUFFICIENT COMBINATION OF SHEAR/SFC-BASED INSTABILITY SHOULD EXIST ALONG THE BOUNDARY AND/OR ALONG PREFRONTAL OUTFLOW TO SUPPORT BANDS/SMALL CLUSTERS OF SUSTAINED STORMS/POSSIBLE SUPERCELLS FROM THE ERN HALF OF OK NEWD INTO MO/NRN AR. BACK/VEER PATTERN IN WIND PROFILES AND DISRUPTED CONVERGENCE FIELD SUGGEST BROKEN QUASI-LINEAR STORM ORGANIZATION. BUT MID LVL LAPSE RATES WILL REMAIN STEEP...AND WHERE HEATING CAN STEEPEN LOW LVL LAPSE RATES/FOCUS LOW LVL CONVERGENCE...SVR WIND AND HAIL LIKELY WILL OCCUR. STILL FARTHER NE ALONG FRONT...SUBSTANTIALLY GREATER /40-50 KT/ DEEP SHEAR WILL EXIST FROM IL/IND INTO LWR MI...ON SRN FRINGE OF DEAMPLIFYING UPR TROUGH. WHILE MID LVL L

sections.text: SLY LLJ SHOULD STRENGTHEN OVER W TX LATE TONIGHT/EARLY TUE ATOP SHALLOW POST-FRONTAL COOL DOME AS A SRN STREAM IMPULSE NOW OFF THE CA CST APPROACHES REGION. GIVEN RICH MOISTURE NOW PRESENT AHEAD OF FRONT...COMBINATION OF INCREASING WAA...ELEVATED MOISTURE INFLUX /MUCAPE TO 1000 J PER KG/...AND 30-40 KT CLOUD LAYER SHEAR MAY SUPPORT A THREAT FOR HAIL AFTER 06Z. ..HALES/GRAMS.. 04/27/2009

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS FAR WRN TX
sections.text: ...TX... PERSISTENT AND SLOW MOVING MCS OVER CENTRAL/SRN TX WAS NOT WELL CAPTURED BY MOST MODELS THIS MORNING. SLIGHT RISK HAS BEEN CUT BACK OVER MUCH OF CENTRAL/NRN TEXAS WHERE CLOUDS/RELATIVELY COOL AIR MASS HAS REDUCED THE CHANCES FOR SEVERE CONVECTION. A SLIGHT RISK HAS BEEN MAINTAINED ACROSS WRN TX WHERE COMBINATION OF STRONG HEATING AND MOIST UPSLOPE SELY WINDS COULD RESULT IN A FEW STORMS ALONG DRYLINE LATE AFTERNOON. OTHER STORMS MAY DEVELOP IN THE TX PANHANDLE AFTER 09Z...DUE TO STRENGTHENING LOW LEVEL JET/WARM ADVECTION.

sections.title: LOWER MI/IN/NWRN OH
sections.text: MODELS ARE CONSISTENT IN SPREADING PCPN NEWD ACROSS THE REGION OVERNIGHT. HOWEVER...A THICK BAND OF CLOUDS WITH MOSTLY LIGHT RAIN SHOWERS WERE SPREADING ACROSS THE AREA FROM THE SW. A WELL MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER...RELATIVELY LARGE SURFACE TEMPERATURE/DEWPOINT SPREADS...WAS RESULTING IN MUCAPES LESS THAN 500 J/KG. THE INCREASING CLOUDS/LIGHT PRECIPITATION DOES NOT BODE WELL FOR SEVERE STORMS. HOWEVER...WILL MAINTAIN LOW WIND PROBS AS THE STRONG ENVIRONMENTAL WIND FIELDS AND INVERTED-V LOW LEVEL SOUNDINGS WOULD FAVOR STRONG WINDS WITH ANY CONVECTIVE STORMS THAT DEVELOP.

sections.title: ERN OK/AR/SRN MO
sections.text: COMBINATION OF MODERATE INSTABILITY...COLD FRONT AND UPPER LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH SHOULD SUPPORT CONTINUED THREAT FOR SEVERE STORMS INTO THE EVENING HOURS. MLCAPES TO 1000 NJ/KG AND 30-40 KT SHEAR INDICATES HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE ARE THE PRIMARY THREATS...SEE WW/S 201 AND 202. ..IMY.. 04/27/2009 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1119 AM CDT MON APR 27 2009/
